source.text: וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֨הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and she said, I have gotten a man with YHWH.

en.L: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and she said, "I have gotten a man with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: The man was intimate with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the help of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I have brought a man into being."
en.R: The man and his wife Eve had a child together. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son named Cain. She said, "With {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s help, I have had a baby boy."

es.L: Y el hombre conoció a Eva su mujer, y ella concibió y dio a luz a Caín, y dijo: «He adquirido un varón con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: El hombre se unió a su esposa Eva, y ella quedó embarazada y dio a luz a Caín. Entonces dijo: «Con la ayuda {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} he dado vida a un hombre».
es.R: El hombre y su esposa Eva tuvieron relaciones, y ella quedó embarazada. Dio a luz a un hijo llamado Caín, y dijo: «Con la ayuda {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} he tenido un hijo varón».

fr.L: Et l’homme connut Ève, sa femme ; elle conçut et enfanta Caïn, et elle dit : « J’ai acquis un homme avec {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: L’homme s’unit à Ève, sa femme ; elle devint enceinte et donna naissance à Caïn. Elle dit : « Avec l’aide {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, j’ai donné la vie à un homme. »
fr.R: L’homme et sa femme Ève ont eu un enfant. Elle est tombée enceinte et elle a mis au monde un fils, appelé Caïn. Elle a dit : « Avec l’aide {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, j’ai eu un petit garçon. »

sw.L: Na yule mtu akamjua Hawa mkewe, naye akapata mimba, akamzaa Kaini, akasema, "Nimempata mwanamume pamoja na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Yule mtu alikutana kimwili na mkewe Hawa, naye akapata mimba, akamzaa Kaini. Akasema, "Kwa msaada wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} nimempata mwanamume."
sw.R: Yule mtu na mkewe Hawa walipata mtoto. Hawa alipata mimba, akamzaa mtoto wa kiume, akamwita Kaini. Akasema, "Kwa msaada wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} nimepata mtoto wa kiume."

decisions.choice: knew: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: "Know" is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union (4:17, 25; 1 Samuel 1:19). It is a personal word, not a crude one.

decisions.choice: Cain ... I have gotten: the name sounds like the verb
decisions.reason: Eve explains the name Cain (qayin) by the verb she uses, "I have gotten" or "I have made" (qaniti). The verb can mean to acquire and also to create (Proverbs 8:22; Deuteronomy 32:6).

decisions.choice: a man with the LORD: with the LORD's help
alternatives: a man, as the LORD did
decisions.reason: The small word "with" (et) can also mark an object, and some have read "I have gotten a man: the LORD", as if Eve thought her son was the promised one of 3:15. But "with" is its usual sense in such a phrase, and the ancient translations read it as help from God. Eve speaks of her son as "a man", a proud word for a newborn, and she names the LORD as the giver of life.

decisions.choice: was intimate with (B); had a child together (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "knew" (m1); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: The divine name is "el SEÑOR" by default, in small capitals as in English, with "Yahvé" as a reader setting. The span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé"), since "Yahvé" takes no article. "Jehová" is a later hybrid form; plain "el Señor" would not show that the name is used.

decisions.choice: un varón (L); un hijo varón (R)
decisions.reason: Eve calls her newborn son "a man" (meaning decision m3). Literal says "varón", the word for a male person, which keeps the wording unusual as it is in Hebrew; Balanced says "un hombre"; Readable "un hijo varón".

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: French narrative tense by level, as the French style guide sets it: the passé simple, the tense of written narrative, at Literal and Balanced ("connut", "donna naissance"), the passé composé of spoken French at Readable ("a mis au monde"). Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level ("j'ai acquis").

source.text: וַתֹּ֣סֶף לָלֶ֔דֶת אֶת־אָחִ֖יו אֶת־הָ֑בֶל וַֽיְהִי־הֶ֨בֶל֙ רֹ֣עֵה צֹ֔אן וְקַ֕יִן הָיָ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ד אֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she added to bear his brother, Abel. And Abel was a shepherd of flock, and Cain was a worker of ground.

en.L: And again she bore his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain was a worker of the ground.
en.B: Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel kept flocks of sheep and goats, and Cain worked the ground.
en.R: Later she had another son, Abel. Abel took care of sheep and goats, and Cain was a farmer.

es.L: Y volvió a dar a luz a su hermano Abel. Y Abel era pastor de ovejas, y Caín era trabajador de la tierra.
es.B: Después dio a luz a Abel, su hermano. Abel cuidaba rebaños de ovejas y cabras, y Caín cultivaba la tierra.
es.R: Más tarde tuvo otro hijo, Abel. Abel cuidaba ovejas y cabras, y Caín era agricultor.

fr.L: Et elle enfanta encore son frère, Abel. Et Abel était berger de moutons, et Caïn était travailleur du sol.
fr.B: Elle donna ensuite naissance à Abel, son frère. Abel gardait des troupeaux de moutons et de chèvres, et Caïn cultivait le sol.
fr.R: Plus tard, elle a eu un autre fils, Abel. Abel s’occupait des moutons et des chèvres, et Caïn était agriculteur.

sw.L: Akamzaa tena nduguye Habili. Naye Habili alikuwa mchungaji wa kondoo, na Kaini alikuwa mkulima wa ardhi.
sw.B: Baadaye akamzaa Habili, ndugu yake. Habili alichunga makundi ya kondoo na mbuzi, na Kaini alilima ardhi.
sw.R: Baadaye Hawa alimzaa mtoto mwingine, Habili. Habili alichunga kondoo na mbuzi, na Kaini alikuwa mkulima.

decisions.choice: Abel (Hevel): a name that means "breath"
decisions.reason: The name is the word for breath or vapor, something that does not last; Ecclesiastes uses it for what is fleeting (Ecclesiastes 1:2). The story gives no explanation of the name, but Abel's life is short.

decisions.choice: keeper of the flock, worker of the ground: the two main ways of life
decisions.reason: The brothers take up the two callings of the ancient world: herding animals and farming. Cain's work is the man's work of 2:15 and 3:23. The text does not favor one way of life over the other.

decisions.choice: flock: sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The word covers small livestock, both sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: again she bore
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "she added to bear", a common way of saying "she did it again".

source.text: וַֽיְהִ֖י מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was from [the] end of days, and brought Cain from [the] fruit of the ground an offering to YHWH.

en.L: And it happened at the end of days that Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: In the course of time Cain brought some of the produce of the ground as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: After some time, Cain brought some of his crops as a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y sucedió al cabo de los días que Caín trajo del fruto de la tierra una ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Con el paso del tiempo, Caín llevó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} una ofrenda de los productos de la tierra.
es.R: Pasado un tiempo, Caín le llevó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} parte de su cosecha como regalo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, au bout des jours, que Caïn apporta du fruit du sol en offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Avec le temps, Caïn apporta des produits du sol en offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Quelque temps après, Caïn a apporté une partie de ses récoltes {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, comme cadeau.

sw.L: Ikawa mwisho wa siku, Kaini akaleta baadhi ya matunda ya ardhi kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Baada ya muda, Kaini alileta baadhi ya mazao ya ardhi kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Baada ya muda fulani, Kaini alimletea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} baadhi ya mazao yake kama zawadi.

decisions.choice: at the end of days: after some time
alternatives: at the end of the year
decisions.reason: The phrase usually means after a period of time, perhaps at the end of a season or a year, when crops were gathered.

decisions.choice: offering: a gift brought to God
alternatives: grain offering (in its later sense only)
decisions.reason: The word means a gift, and it is used for tribute to a king (32:13) as well as for gifts to God. In the laws of Leviticus it names the grain offering; here it is used of both brothers' gifts, plants and animals alike.

source.text: וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן וַיִּ֣שַׁע יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הֶ֖בֶל וְאֶל־מִנְחָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abel brought, also he, from [the] firstborn of his flock and from their fat [portions]. And looked YHWH to Abel and to his offering,

en.L: And Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat portions. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked with favor on Abel and on his offering,
en.B: And Abel also brought an offering: some of the firstborn of his flock, with their fat portions. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
en.R: Abel also brought a gift. He chose some of the first lambs born in his flock and offered their best parts. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was pleased with Abel and his gift,

es.L: Y Abel trajo también él de los primogénitos de su rebaño, y de la grasa de ellos. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} miró con agrado a Abel y a su ofrenda,
es.B: También Abel llevó una ofrenda: algunas de las primeras crías de su rebaño, con su grasa. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} miró con agrado a Abel y su ofrenda,
es.R: Abel también llevó un regalo. Escogió algunos de los primeros corderos que nacieron en su rebaño y ofreció las mejores partes. {{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} le agradaron Abel y su regalo,

fr.L: Et Abel, lui aussi, apporta des premiers-nés de son troupeau et de leur graisse. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} porta un regard favorable sur Abel et sur son offrande,
fr.B: Abel, lui aussi, apporta une offrande : quelques-uns des premiers-nés de son troupeau, avec leurs parties grasses. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accueillit avec faveur Abel et son offrande,
fr.R: Abel aussi a apporté un cadeau. Il a choisi quelques-uns des premiers agneaux nés dans son troupeau, et il en a offert les meilleurs morceaux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a été content d’Abel et de son cadeau,

sw.L: Naye Habili pia akaleta baadhi ya wazaliwa wa kwanza wa kundi lake na baadhi ya mafuta yao. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtazama kwa kibali Habili na sadaka yake,
sw.B: Habili naye alileta sadaka: baadhi ya wazaliwa wa kwanza wa kundi lake, pamoja na sehemu zao za mafuta. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamkubali Habili na sadaka yake,
sw.R: Habili pia alileta zawadi. Alichagua baadhi ya wana-kondoo wa kwanza waliozaliwa katika kundi lake, akatoa sehemu zao zilizo bora. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipendezwa na Habili na zawadi yake,

decisions.choice: the firstborn of his flock and their fat: the first and the best
decisions.reason: The firstborn of the flock and the fat portions were counted as the best and as belonging to God (Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Abel's gift is described with care; Cain's simply as "some of the fruit" (verse 3), not the first fruits.

decisions.choice: looked with favor: accepted
decisions.reason: The verb means to look at, here with favor. The story does not say how Cain and Abel knew which offering was accepted.

decisions.choice: their best parts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fat portions stood for (m1): the best of the animal.

decisions.choice: las primeras crías de su rebaño
decisions.reason: In modern Spanish "primogénito" is used mainly of people. Literal keeps it, the word of the laws on the firstborn (meaning decision m1); Balanced says what it means for a flock.

en.B: but on Cain and his offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.
en.R: but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not pleased with Cain and his gift. Cain became very angry, and he looked upset.

es.L: pero a Caín y a su ofrenda no los miró con agrado. Y Caín se enojó mucho, y se abatió su rostro.
es.B: pero a Caín y su ofrenda no los miró con agrado. Por eso Caín se enfureció, y su rostro quedó abatido.
es.R: pero Caín y su regalo no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agradaron. Caín se enojó mucho, y se le veía molesto.

fr.B: mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’accueillit pas avec faveur Caïn et son offrande. Caïn en fut très irrité, et son visage s’assombrit.
fr.R: mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas été content de Caïn et de son cadeau. Caïn s’est mis très en colère, et il avait l’air contrarié.

sw.L: lakini kwa Kaini na kwa sadaka yake hakutazama kwa kibali. Naye Kaini akakasirika sana, uso wake ukainama.
sw.B: lakini hakumkubali Kaini wala sadaka yake. Basi Kaini akakasirika sana, uso wake ukakunjamana.
sw.R: lakini hakupendezwa na Kaini wala zawadi yake. Kaini alikasirika sana, akakunja uso.

decisions.choice: Cain's offering not accepted: the reason is not stated
alternatives: because grain was the wrong kind of offering
because Cain's heart was not right
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. It describes Abel's gift as the first and best (verse 4) and Cain's more plainly, and it says God looked on Abel and Cain themselves as well as on their gifts. Hebrews 11:4 says Abel offered "by faith", and 1 John 3:12 that Cain's own deeds were evil. Grain offerings were acceptable in Israel's law, so the kind of gift is not likely the reason.

decisions.choice: it burned to Cain: Cain was furious
decisions.reason: Anger is described as burning in Hebrew. "His face fell" pictures sullen anger or dejection.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־קָ֑יִן לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why do you look so upset?

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Caín: «¿Por qué te has enojado, y por qué se ha abatido tu rostro?
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Caín: «¿Por qué estás enojado? ¿Por qué tienes el rostro abatido?
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Caín: «¿Por qué estás enojado? ¿Por qué estás tan molesto?

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Caïn : « Pourquoi es-tu irrité, et pourquoi ton visage s’est-il abattu ?
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Caïn : « Pourquoi es-tu irrité ? Pourquoi ce visage sombre ?
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Caïn : « Pourquoi es-tu en colère ? Pourquoi as-tu l’air si contrarié ?

sw.B: Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Kaini, "Kwa nini umekasirika? Kwa nini uso wako umekunjamana?
sw.R: Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwuliza Kaini, "Kwa nini umekasirika? Kwa nini umekunja uso hivyo?

decisions.choice: why ...? why ...?: God speaks to Cain before he acts
decisions.reason: As with the man and woman in chapter 3, God speaks with Cain by asking questions. This time he speaks before the wrong is done, to warn him (verse 7).

source.text: הֲל֤וֹא אִם־תֵּיטִיב֙ שְׂאֵ֔ת וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תֵיטִ֔יב לַפֶּ֖תַח חַטָּ֣את רֹבֵ֑ץ וְאֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָת֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּמְשָׁל־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is [it] not, if you do well, lifting up? And if you do not do well, at the door sin [is] crouching, and to you [is] its desire, and you, you must rule over it.

en.L: If you do well, [will there] not [be] lifting up? And if you do not do well, sin [is] crouching at the door, and its desire [is] for you, but you must rule over it."
en.B: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door. It wants to have you, but you must master it."
en.R: If you do what is right, I will accept you. But if you do not do what is right, sin is waiting to attack you, like an animal crouching by the door. Sin wants to control you, but you must control it."

es.L: Si haces bien, ¿no [serás] levantado? Y si no haces bien, el pecado [está] agazapado a la puerta, y hacia ti [va] su deseo, pero tú debes dominarlo».
es.B: Si obras bien, ¿no serás aceptado? Pero si no obras bien, el pecado está agazapado a tu puerta. Quiere apoderarse de ti, pero tú debes dominarlo».
es.R: Si haces lo correcto, te aceptaré. Pero si no haces lo correcto, el pecado te está esperando para atacarte, como un animal escondido junto a la puerta, listo para saltar. El pecado quiere dominarte, pero tú debes dominarlo a él».

fr.L: Si tu agis bien, [n’y aura-t-il] pas [un] relèvement ? Et si tu n’agis pas bien, le péché [est] tapi à la porte, et vers toi [va] son désir, mais toi, tu dois le dominer. »
fr.B: Si tu fais ce qui est bien, ne seras-tu pas accepté ? Mais si tu ne fais pas ce qui est bien, le péché est tapi à ta porte. Il cherche à s’emparer de toi, mais toi, tu dois le maîtriser. »
fr.R: Si tu fais ce qui est bien, je t’accepterai. Mais si tu ne fais pas ce qui est bien, le péché t’attend pour t’attaquer, comme une bête couchée près de la porte. Le péché veut te dominer, mais c’est toi qui dois le dominer. »

sw.L: Ukitenda mema, je, [hakutakuwa na] kuinuliwa? Na usipotenda mema, dhambi inaotea mlangoni, na tamaa yake [ni] kwako, lakini wewe unapaswa kuitawala."
sw.B: Ukitenda yaliyo mema, je, hutakubaliwa? Lakini usipotenda yaliyo mema, dhambi inakuotea mlangoni pako. Inataka kukutawala, lakini wewe lazima uishinde."
sw.R: Ukitenda yaliyo mema, nitakukubali. Lakini usipotenda yaliyo mema, dhambi inakuvizia ili ikushambulie, kama mnyama aliyejificha karibu na mlango. Dhambi inataka kukutawala, lakini wewe lazima uitawale."

decisions.choice: lifting up: being accepted, with your face lifted up
decisions.reason: "Lifting up" answers "your face has fallen" (verse 6): if Cain does well, his face will be lifted, he will be accepted and at peace. The same word can be used for lifting away guilt (forgiveness), which may also be in view.

decisions.choice: sin is crouching at the door: sin is pictured like an animal lying in wait
alternatives: a sin offering lies at the door
decisions.reason: Sin is pictured as a beast crouching at the entrance, ready to spring. The verb is used for animals lying down (29:2; 49:9). Here, for the first time in the Bible, the word "sin" appears.

decisions.choice: its desire is for you, but you must rule over it: the words of 3:16
alternatives: its desire is for you, and you will rule over it (a promise)
decisions.reason: The words repeat 3:16 ("your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you"). Here sin wants to master Cain, and he is called to master it. The verb form can be a command ("you must") or a promise ("you will"); in the warning, a command or a call fits best.

decisions.choice: like an animal crouching by the door
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the crouching beast and says what it means (m2).

decisions.choice: ¿no [serás] levantado?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a noun, "lifting up", which answers the fallen face of verse 6 (meaning decision m1). Spanish nouns for it ("levantamiento", "alzamiento") mean an uprising, so Literal uses the verb "levantado", which keeps the picture of being lifted up and accepted. A reviewer may prefer a wording that names the face.

decisions.choice: agazapado (L, B); como un animal escondido junto a la puerta, listo para saltar (R)
decisions.reason: "Agazapado" is used of an animal crouched low and ready to spring, the picture of meaning decision m2. Readable spells out the picture in common words, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: tapi
decisions.reason: The verb (rovets) is used of animals lying down (m2). "Tapi" says lying low and hidden, ready to spring, which keeps the picture of the beast at the door; "couché" would say only that sin is lying there.

decisions.choice: inaotea (L), inakuotea (B)
decisions.reason: The verb (rovets) is used of animals lying down (m2). "Kuotea" is to lie in wait for prey, which keeps the picture of the beast at the door; Readable says "inakuvizia ... kama mnyama", as the English Readable explains it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יו וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּהְיוֹתָ֣ם בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּ֥קָם קַ֛יִן אֶל־הֶ֥בֶל אָחִ֖יו וַיַּהַרְגֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Cain to Abel his brother. And it was, when they were in the field, and rose up Cain against Abel his brother and killed him.

en.L: And Cain said to Abel his brother ... And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
en.B: Cain spoke to his brother Abel. And while they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.
en.R: Cain spoke to his brother Abel. While they were out in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

es.L: Y dijo Caín a Abel su hermano ... Y cuando estaban en el campo, se levantó Caín contra Abel su hermano y lo mató.
es.B: Caín habló con su hermano Abel. Y mientras estaban en el campo, Caín atacó a su hermano Abel y lo mató.
es.R: Caín habló con su hermano Abel. Cuando estaban afuera, en el campo, Caín atacó a su hermano Abel y lo mató.

fr.L: Et Caïn dit à Abel son frère ... Et comme ils étaient dans le champ, Caïn se leva contre Abel son frère et le tua.
fr.B: Caïn parla à son frère Abel. Et pendant qu’ils étaient dans les champs, Caïn se jeta sur son frère Abel et le tua.
fr.R: Caïn a parlé à son frère Abel. Pendant qu’ils étaient dehors, dans les champs, Caïn a attaqué son frère Abel et l’a tué.

sw.L: Naye Kaini akamwambia Habili ndugu yake ... Ikawa walipokuwa shambani, Kaini akainuka dhidi ya Habili ndugu yake, akamuua.
sw.B: Kaini akazungumza na ndugu yake Habili. Walipokuwa shambani, Kaini akamvamia ndugu yake Habili, akamuua.
sw.R: Kaini alizungumza na ndugu yake Habili. Walipokuwa nje shambani, Kaini alimshambulia ndugu yake Habili, akamuua.

decisions.choice: Cain said to Abel his brother: the Hebrew text gives no words
alternatives: Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go out to the field (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac, Latin)
decisions.reason: The verb "said" normally introduces words, but in the Hebrew text nothing follows. The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, the Syriac and the Latin have "Let us go out to the field", which may have dropped out of the Hebrew. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: rose up against his brother and killed him: the first murder
decisions.reason: "Brother" is repeated through the chapter (seven times in verses 2-11): the first murder is the killing of a brother. Jesus speaks of "the blood of righteous Abel" (Matthew 23:35), and 1 John 3:12 warns not to be like Cain.

decisions.choice: Cain said to Abel his brother ...
decisions.reason: Literal marks the gap in the Hebrew text with an ellipsis (m1).

decisions.choice: Cain spoke to his brother Abel
alternatives: Cain said to his brother Abel
decisions.reason: Since the Hebrew gives no words (m1), Balanced and Readable say "spoke to", which needs none.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־קַ֔יִן אֵ֖י הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי הֲשֹׁמֵ֥ר אָחִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to Cain, where [is] Abel your brother? And he said, I do not know; [the] keeper of my brother [am] I?

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Where [is] Abel your brother?" And he said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I do not know," he answered. "Am I my brother's keeper?"
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asked Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain answered, "I do not know. Is it my job to take care of my brother?"

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Caín: «¿Dónde [está] Abel tu hermano?». Y él dijo: «No sé. ¿Soy yo el guardián de mi hermano?».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le preguntó a Caín: «¿Dónde está tu hermano Abel?». «No lo sé», respondió. «¿Acaso soy yo el guardián de mi hermano?».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le preguntó a Caín: «¿Dónde está tu hermano Abel?». Caín respondió: «No lo sé. ¿Acaso me toca a mí cuidar a mi hermano?».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Caïn : « Où [est] Abel ton frère ? » Et il dit : « Je ne sais pas. Suis-je le gardien de mon frère, moi ? »
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Caïn : « Où est ton frère Abel ? » « Je n’en sais rien, répondit-il. Est-ce que je suis le gardien de mon frère ? »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a demandé à Caïn : « Où est ton frère Abel ? » Caïn a répondu : « Je ne sais pas. Est-ce que c’est mon travail de m’occuper de mon frère ? »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Kaini, "Habili ndugu yako [yuko] wapi?" Naye akasema, "Sijui. Je, mimi ni mlinzi wa ndugu yangu?"
sw.B: Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwuliza Kaini, "Ndugu yako Habili yuko wapi?" Akajibu, "Sijui. Kwani mimi ni mlinzi wa ndugu yangu?"
sw.R: Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwuliza Kaini, "Ndugu yako Habili yuko wapi?" Kaini akajibu, "Sijui. Je, ni kazi yangu kumtunza ndugu yangu?"

decisions.choice: where is Abel your brother?: God's question echoes "where are you?" (3:9)
decisions.reason: As God asked the man "where are you?", he asks Cain about his brother, giving him the chance to confess. Cain answers with a lie and a question.

decisions.choice: my brother's keeper: one who watches over him
decisions.reason: "Keeper" is from the verb "keep" in 2:15, used for the man's care of the garden. Cain's question rejects any duty toward his brother.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ ק֚וֹל דְּמֵ֣י אָחִ֔יךָ צֹעֲקִ֥ים אֵלַ֖י מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, what have you done? [The] voice of [the] bloods of your brother [is] crying to me from the ground.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood is crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "What have you done? Your brother's blood is calling out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the ground, asking for justice.

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Qué has hecho? La voz de la sangre de tu hermano clama a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} desde la tierra.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «¿Qué has hecho? ¡Escucha! La sangre de tu hermano clama a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} desde la tierra.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «¿Qué has hecho? Desde la tierra, la sangre de tu hermano grita a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y pide justicia.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Qu’as-tu fait ? La voix du sang de ton frère crie vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis le sol.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Qu’as-tu fait ? Écoute ! Le sang de ton frère crie vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis la terre.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : « Qu’as-tu fait ? Depuis la terre, le sang de ton frère {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelle et réclame justice.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Umefanya nini? Sauti ya damu ya ndugu yako inanililia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kutoka ardhini.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Umefanya nini? Sikiliza! Damu ya ndugu yako inanililia kutoka ardhini.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Umefanya nini? Damu ya ndugu yako inaniita kutoka ardhini, ikidai haki.

decisions.choice: the voice of your brother's blood is crying out: the murdered man's blood calls for justice
decisions.reason: "Blood" is plural here, as often for shed blood. The verb is used for the cry of the oppressed for help and justice (Exodus 3:7; 22:23). The blood itself cries out from the ground; Hebrews 12:24 contrasts it with the blood of Jesus, "which speaks a better word".

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, the LORD of verse 9; Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: Listen!
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "the voice of" into a call to hear, as the Hebrew word can mean ("Hark!").

decisions.choice: asking for justice
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blood's cry is for (m1).

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אָר֣וּר אָ֑תָּה מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּצְתָ֣ה אֶת־פִּ֔יהָ לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־דְּמֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now cursed [are] you from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive the bloods of your brother from your hand.

en.L: And now you [are] cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
en.B: Now you are cursed, driven from the ground that opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
en.R: Now you are under a curse, and the ground will no longer be your home. It opened up to soak in your brother's blood, which you spilled.

es.L: Y ahora tú [eres] maldito desde la tierra, que ha abierto su boca para recibir de tu mano la sangre de tu hermano.
es.B: Ahora quedas bajo maldición, desterrado de la tierra que abrió su boca para recibir de tu mano la sangre de tu hermano.
es.R: Ahora estás bajo una maldición, y la tierra ya no será tu hogar. Se abrió para beber la sangre de tu hermano, la sangre que tú derramaste.

fr.L: Et maintenant, tu [es] maudit, loin du sol qui a ouvert sa bouche pour recevoir de ta main le sang de ton frère.
fr.B: Maintenant, tu es maudit et chassé du sol qui a ouvert la bouche pour recevoir de ta main le sang de ton frère.
fr.R: Maintenant, tu es sous une malédiction, et la terre ne sera plus ta maison. Elle s’est ouverte pour boire le sang de ton frère, que tu as versé.

sw.L: Na sasa umelaaniwa, mbali na ardhi iliyofungua kinywa chake kupokea damu ya ndugu yako kutoka mkononi mwako.
sw.B: Sasa umelaaniwa, umefukuzwa kutoka katika ardhi iliyofungua kinywa chake kupokea damu ya ndugu yako kutoka mkononi mwako.
sw.R: Sasa uko chini ya laana, na ardhi haitakuwa tena makao yako. Ilifunguka ikanywa damu ya ndugu yako, uliyoimwaga wewe.

decisions.choice: cursed from the ground: cursed, and driven away from it
decisions.reason: "From" can mean "away from": Cain will be cut off from the ground he worked (verse 12) and driven from it (verse 14). In 3:17 the ground was cursed; now Cain himself is cursed, the first human being to be cursed.

decisions.choice: the ground opened its mouth: the earth drank the blood
decisions.reason: The ground is pictured as a mouth that took in Abel's blood, and so is a witness to the crime.

decisions.choice: tu [es] maudit, loin du sol
decisions.reason: "Maudit du sol" would read in French as "cursed by the ground". Literal keeps "from" in its sense "away from" (m1) with "loin du sol"; Balanced says "maudit et chassé du sol".

source.text: כִּ֤י תַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹֽא־תֹסֵ֥ף תֵּת־כֹּחָ֖הּ לָ֑ךְ נָ֥ע וָנָ֖ד תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה בָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you work the ground, it will not again give its strength to you. A wanderer and a fugitive you will be on the earth.

en.L: When you work the ground, it will no longer give its strength to you; you will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth."
en.B: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."
en.R: When you farm the land, it will not grow good crops for you anymore. You will wander from place to place, with no home on earth."

es.L: Cuando trabajes la tierra, no volverá a darte su fuerza; errante y fugitivo serás en la tierra».
es.B: Cuando cultives la tierra, ya no te dará sus frutos. Andarás errante y sin descanso por la tierra».
es.R: Cuando siembres la tierra, ya no te dará buenas cosechas. Andarás de un lugar a otro, sin tener hogar en ningún lugar».

fr.L: Quand tu travailleras le sol, il ne te donnera plus sa force ; tu seras errant et fugitif sur la terre. »
fr.B: Quand tu cultiveras le sol, il ne te donnera plus ses récoltes. Tu seras un homme sans repos, toujours errant sur la terre. »
fr.R: Quand tu cultiveras la terre, elle ne te donnera plus de bonnes récoltes. Tu iras d’un endroit à l’autre, sans maison sur la terre. »

sw.L: Utakapolima ardhi, haitakupa tena nguvu zake; utakuwa mzururaji na mkimbizi duniani."
sw.B: Utakapolima ardhi, haitakuzalia tena mazao yake. Utakuwa mtu asiyetulia, anayezunguka-zunguka duniani."
sw.R: Utakapolima shamba, halitakuzalia tena mavuno mazuri. Utatangatanga kutoka mahali hadi mahali, bila makao duniani."

decisions.choice: its strength: its produce
decisions.reason: The ground's "strength" is what it produces. For a farmer like Cain, this is the end of his work.

decisions.choice: a wanderer and a fugitive: restless, without a settled home
decisions.reason: The two words sound alike (na wa-nad) and together mean someone always on the move, without rest or home. The second returns in the name of the land Cain goes to, Nod (verse 16).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל עֲוֺנִ֖י מִנְּשֹֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Cain to YHWH, great [is] my punishment from bearing.

en.L: And Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "My punishment [is] too great to bear.
en.B: Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "My punishment is more than I can bear.
en.R: Cain said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "This punishment is too much for me to bear.

es.L: Y dijo Caín {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Mi castigo [es] demasiado grande para soportarlo.
es.B: Caín dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Mi castigo es más de lo que puedo soportar.
es.R: Caín le dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Este castigo es demasiado para mí; no lo puedo soportar.

fr.L: Et Caïn dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Mon châtiment [est] trop grand pour [être] porté.
fr.B: Caïn dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Ma punition est plus lourde que je ne peux le supporter.
fr.R: Caïn a dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Cette punition est trop dure pour moi, je ne peux pas la supporter.

sw.L: Naye Kaini akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Adhabu yangu [ni] kubwa mno kuibeba.
sw.B: Kaini akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Adhabu yangu ni zaidi ya ninavyoweza kuvumilia.
sw.R: Kaini akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Adhabu hii ni nzito mno kwangu; siwezi kuivumilia.

decisions.choice: my punishment is too great to bear
alternatives: my guilt is too great to be forgiven
decisions.reason: The word means both guilt and the punishment that guilt brings, and the verb "bear" can also mean "take away" (forgive). So the line can be read as "my guilt is too great to be forgiven". Cain's next words (verse 14) complain of what will happen to him, which favors "punishment".

source.text: הֵן֩ גֵּרַ֨שְׁתָּ אֹתִ֜י הַיּ֗וֹם מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וּמִפָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶסָּתֵ֑ר וְהָיִ֜יתִי נָ֤ע וָנָד֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה כָל־מֹצְאִ֖י יַֽהַרְגֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Behold, you have driven me today from on [the] face of the ground, and from your face I will be hidden, and I will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and it will be [that] everyone who finds me will kill me.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have driven me today from the face of the ground, and from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face I will be hidden; and I will be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
en.B: Today {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
en.R: Today {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are sending me away from my land, and I will not be near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anymore. I will wander from place to place, and anyone who finds me will kill me."

es.L: Mira, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me has echado hoy de la faz de la tierra, y de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rostro quedaré oculto; y seré errante y fugitivo en la tierra, y cualquiera que me encuentre me matará».
es.B: Hoy {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me estás echando de esta tierra, y quedaré oculto de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} presencia. Andaré errante y sin descanso por la tierra, y cualquiera que me encuentre me matará».
es.R: Hoy me estás echando de mi tierra, y ya no estaré cerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Andaré de un lugar a otro, y cualquiera que me encuentre me matará».

fr.L: Voici, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as chassé aujourd’hui de la face du sol, et je serai caché loin de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face ; je serai errant et fugitif sur la terre, et quiconque me trouvera me tuera. »
fr.B: Aujourd’hui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me chasses de ce pays, et je serai caché loin de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} présence. Je serai un homme sans repos, errant sur la terre, et le premier qui me trouvera me tuera. »
fr.R: Aujourd’hui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me renvoies loin de ma terre, et je ne serai plus près de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. J’irai d’un endroit à l’autre, et n’importe qui pourra me trouver et me tuer. »

sw.L: Tazama, umenifukuza leo kutoka katika uso wa ardhi, nami nitafichwa mbali na uso {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}; nami nitakuwa mzururaji na mkimbizi duniani, na kila atakayenipata ataniua."
sw.B: Leo unanifukuza kutoka katika nchi hii, nami nitafichwa mbali na uwepo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Nitakuwa mtu asiyetulia, nikizunguka-zunguka duniani, na yeyote atakayenikuta ataniua."
sw.R: Leo unanifukuza kutoka katika nchi yangu, wala sitakuwa karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} tena. Nitatangatanga kutoka mahali hadi mahali, na yeyote atakayenikuta ataniua."

decisions.choice: hidden from your face: shut out of God's presence
decisions.reason: To be hidden from God's face is to lose his care and protection (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; Psalm 27:9). Cain sees that being driven from the land means being driven from God.

decisions.choice: whoever finds me will kill me: other people are assumed
decisions.reason: The story assumes there are other people who might avenge Abel. It does not say who they are; the account follows one family line and says elsewhere that Adam had other sons and daughters (5:4).

decisions.choice: you, your (lowercase by default; You, Your with the setting)
decisions.reason: Cain speaks to God, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: uso {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} (L), uwepo {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} (B), karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} (R)
alternatives: no span, since "you" is a verb prefix in "umenifukuza"
decisions.reason: Cain speaks to God. The "you" of "you have driven me" is the prefix of the verb, which takes no span; the free possessive "wako" and the joined pronoun "nawe" do.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כָּל־הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהוָ֤ה לְקַ֨יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־מֹצְאֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him YHWH, therefore anyone who kills Cain, sevenfold he will be avenged. And set YHWH for Cain a sign, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Therefore whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set a sign for Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Because of this, whoever kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over." Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Because of that, if anyone kills Cain, I will punish that person seven times as much." So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put a mark on Cain to warn anyone who found him not to kill him.

es.L: Y le dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «Por tanto, cualquiera que mate a Caín, de él se tomará venganza siete veces». Y puso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} una señal a Caín, para que nadie que lo encontrara lo hiriera.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Por eso, quien mate a Caín sufrirá una venganza siete veces mayor». Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso una marca en Caín, para que nadie que lo encontrara lo matara.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Por eso, si alguien mata a Caín, castigaré a esa persona siete veces más». Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le puso una marca a Caín, para advertir a cualquiera que lo encontrara que no lo matara.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « C’est pourquoi, quiconque tuera Caïn, sur lui on se vengera sept fois. » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mit un signe pour Caïn, afin que quiconque le trouverait ne le frappe pas.
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit : « Pour cette raison, celui qui tuera Caïn subira une vengeance sept fois plus grande. » Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mit une marque sur Caïn, pour que personne, en le trouvant, ne le tue.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : « À cause de cela, si quelqu’un tue Caïn, je punirai cette personne sept fois plus. » Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a mis une marque sur Caïn, pour avertir tous ceux qui le trouveraient de ne pas le tuer.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Kwa hiyo, yeyote atakayemuua Kaini, atalipizwa kisasi mara saba." Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwekea Kaini ishara, ili yeyote atakayemkuta asimpige.
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Kwa sababu hiyo, yeyote atakayemuua Kaini atalipizwa kisasi mara saba zaidi." Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtia Kaini alama, ili mtu yeyote atakayemkuta asimuue.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Kwa sababu hiyo, mtu yeyote akimuua Kaini, nitamwadhibu mtu huyo mara saba zaidi." Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwekea Kaini alama, ili kumwonya kila atakayemkuta asimuue.

decisions.choice: therefore, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "therefore" (laken); the Septuagint, the Syriac and the Latin read "not so" (lo ken), which differs by one letter and answers Cain's fear more directly. The Hebrew text is followed here: because Cain fears for his life, God protects him.

decisions.choice: sevenfold: in full measure
decisions.reason: Seven is a number of completeness. Vengeance "sevenfold" means full and severe vengeance. God's protection limits violence instead of letting it run on, though Lamech will boast of more (verse 24).

decisions.choice: a sign: a mark or token that protected Cain
alternatives: a sign given to Cain to reassure him
decisions.reason: The word means a sign or token (9:12; Exodus 12:13). The text does not say what it was or whether it was on Cain's body; it served to protect him.

decisions.choice: Because of this (B); Because of that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "because of this" to tie God's answer to Cain's fear (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּ֥צֵא קַ֖יִן מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־נ֖וֹד קִדְמַת־עֵֽדֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Cain from before YHWH and dwelt in [the] land of Nod, east of Eden.

en.L: And Cain went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
en.B: So Cain went out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
en.R: So Cain left the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was near and went to live in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

es.L: Y salió Caín de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y vivió en la tierra de Nod, al este de Edén.
es.B: Así Caín se alejó de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se estableció en la tierra de Nod, al este de Edén.
es.R: Entonces Caín dejó el lugar donde {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba cerca y se fue a vivir a la tierra de Nod, al este de Edén.

fr.L: Et Caïn sortit de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et habita au pays de Nod, à l’orient d’Éden.
fr.B: Caïn s’éloigna donc de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et s’établit au pays de Nod, à l’est d’Éden.
fr.R: Alors Caïn a quitté l’endroit où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était proche, et il est allé vivre dans le pays de Nod, à l’est d’Éden.

sw.L: Naye Kaini akatoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akakaa katika nchi ya Nodi, mashariki ya Edeni.
sw.B: Basi Kaini akaondoka mbele ya uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akaishi katika nchi ya Nodi, upande wa mashariki wa Edeni.
sw.R: Basi Kaini akaondoka mahali ambapo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa karibu, akaenda kuishi katika nchi ya Nodi, mashariki ya Edeni.

decisions.choice: Nod: "wandering"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the word for "fugitive" in verses 12 and 14: Cain settles in the Land of Wandering. No place of that name is known.

decisions.choice: east of Eden: further from the garden
decisions.reason: The man and the woman were sent out to the east of the garden (3:24); Cain goes further east still. Later in Genesis, going east marks moving away from God's blessing (11:2; 13:11).

source.text: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֨יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־חֲנ֑וֹךְ וַֽיְהִי֙ בֹּ֣נֶה עִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And knew Cain his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city according to the name of his son, Enoch.

en.L: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
en.B: Cain was intimate with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was building a city, and he named it Enoch, after his son.
en.R: Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. Cain was building a city at that time, and he named it Enoch, after his son.

es.L: Y conoció Caín a su mujer, y ella concibió y dio a luz a Enoc. Y él estaba edificando una ciudad, y llamó el nombre de la ciudad según el nombre de su hijo, Enoc.
es.B: Caín se unió a su esposa, y ella quedó embarazada y dio a luz a Enoc. Caín estaba construyendo una ciudad, y le puso el nombre de su hijo, Enoc.
es.R: Caín y su esposa tuvieron un hijo llamado Enoc. En ese tiempo Caín estaba construyendo una ciudad, y le puso Enoc, como su hijo.

fr.L: Et Caïn connut sa femme ; elle conçut et enfanta Hénoch. Et il était en train de bâtir une ville, et il appela le nom de la ville d’après le nom de son fils, Hénoch.
fr.B: Caïn s’unit à sa femme ; elle devint enceinte et donna naissance à Hénoch. Caïn bâtissait une ville, et il lui donna le nom de son fils, Hénoch.
fr.R: Caïn et sa femme ont eu un fils, appelé Hénoch. À cette époque, Caïn construisait une ville, et il l’a appelée Hénoch, comme son fils.

sw.L: Naye Kaini akamjua mkewe, naye akapata mimba, akamzaa Henoko. Naye alikuwa akijenga mji, akauita jina la mji kwa jina la mwanawe, Henoko.
sw.B: Kaini alikutana kimwili na mkewe, naye akapata mimba, akamzaa Henoko. Kaini alikuwa akijenga mji, akauita Henoko, kwa jina la mwanawe.
sw.R: Kaini na mkewe walipata mtoto wa kiume, wakamwita Henoko. Wakati huo Kaini alikuwa akijenga mji, akauita Henoko, kwa jina la mwanawe.

decisions.choice: his wife: not explained
decisions.reason: The story does not say who Cain's wife was. Adam had other sons and daughters (5:4), and in the first generations marriage within the family is assumed.

decisions.choice: he was building a city: Cain, or possibly Enoch
alternatives: Enoch was building a city, named after his son Irad
decisions.reason: The natural reading is that Cain built the city and named it after his son. Some read Enoch as the builder, which would explain the unusual wording "according to the name of his son".

decisions.choice: a city: the wanderer builds a settled place
decisions.reason: Cain was sentenced to wander, yet he builds a city, the first in the Bible. The line of Cain goes on to found the arts of civilization (verses 20-22).

source.text: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּמְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־לָֽמֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was born to Enoch Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehijael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.

en.L: And to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
en.B: Enoch had a son named Irad, Irad was the father of Mehujael, Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.
en.R: Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad was the father of Mehujael. Mehujael was the father of Methushael. Methushael was the father of Lamech.

es.L: Y a Enoc le nació Irad, e Irad engendró a Mehujael, y Mehujael engendró a Metusael, y Metusael engendró a Lamec.
es.B: Enoc tuvo un hijo llamado Irad; Irad fue el padre de Mehujael, Mehujael fue el padre de Metusael, y Metusael fue el padre de Lamec.
es.R: Enoc tuvo un hijo llamado Irad. Irad fue el padre de Mehujael. Mehujael fue el padre de Metusael. Metusael fue el padre de Lamec.

fr.L: Et à Hénoch naquit Irad, et Irad engendra Mehujaël, et Mehujaël engendra Metushaël, et Metushaël engendra Lamech.
fr.B: Hénoch eut un fils, Irad ; Irad fut le père de Mehujaël, Mehujaël celui de Metushaël, et Metushaël celui de Lamech.
fr.R: Hénoch a eu un fils appelé Irad. Irad a été le père de Mehujaël. Mehujaël a été le père de Metushaël. Metushaël a été le père de Lamech.

sw.L: Naye Henoko akapata mwana, Iradi, naye Iradi akamzaa Mehuyaeli, naye Mehuyaeli akamzaa Methushaeli, naye Methushaeli akamzaa Lameki.
sw.B: Henoko alimzaa Iradi; Iradi akawa baba wa Mehuyaeli, Mehuyaeli akawa baba wa Methushaeli, na Methushaeli akawa baba wa Lameki.
sw.R: Henoko alipata mtoto wa kiume, Iradi. Iradi alikuwa baba wa Mehuyaeli. Mehuyaeli alikuwa baba wa Methushaeli. Methushaeli alikuwa baba wa Lameki.

decisions.choice: Mehujael: the name is spelled two ways in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes the name Mehujael the first time and Mehijael the second. Translations use one form; the meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: Lamech: not the Lamech of 5:25-31
decisions.reason: This Lamech, of Cain's line, is not the father of Noah in Seth's line (5:28-29). Some names in the two lines are alike (Enoch, Lamech; Irad and Jared; Methushael and Methuselah).

decisions.choice: Irad, Mehujael, Metusael, Lamec
decisions.reason: Traditional Spanish forms of the names, with one spelling for Mehujael (meaning decision m1). "Metusael" is kept distinct from "Matusalén" of Seth's line (5:21), as the Hebrew names differ (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Irad, Mehujaël, Metushaël, Lamech
decisions.reason: Names with no settled French form are transcribed as the English does, with the French diaeresis on "-ël". "Lamech" is the form already used in Luke 3:36 and, like "Hénoch" (Hebrews 11:5, Jude 14), is kept for both men of the name (4:18; 5:25).

decisions.choice: Iradi, Mehuyaeli, Methushaeli, Lameki
decisions.reason: Swahili forms ending in a vowel, with "y" for the Hebrew "j" sound as in "Yakobo". "Lameki" and "Henoko" are the forms already used in Luke 3:36-37 and Hebrews 11:5, and are kept for both men of the name (4:18; 5:25).

source.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ לֶ֖מֶךְ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took for himself Lamech two wives; [the] name of the one [was] Adah, and [the] name of the second [was] Zillah.

en.L: And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of the one [was] Adah, and the name of the second [was] Zillah.
en.B: Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
en.R: Lamech married two women. One was named Adah, and the other was named Zillah.

es.L: Y tomó Lamec para sí dos mujeres; el nombre de la una [era] Ada, y el nombre de la segunda [era] Zila.
es.B: Lamec se casó con dos mujeres: una se llamaba Ada, y la otra, Zila.
es.R: Lamec se casó con dos mujeres. Una se llamaba Ada, y la otra se llamaba Zila.

fr.L: Et Lamech prit pour lui deux femmes ; le nom de l’une [était] Ada, et le nom de la seconde [était] Tsilla.
fr.B: Lamech épousa deux femmes, l’une appelée Ada et l’autre Tsilla.
fr.R: Lamech s’est marié avec deux femmes. L’une s’appelait Ada, et l’autre s’appelait Tsilla.

sw.L: Naye Lameki akajitwalia wake wawili; jina la mmoja [lilikuwa] Ada, na jina la wa pili [lilikuwa] Sila.
sw.B: Lameki alioa wanawake wawili, mmoja aliitwa Ada na mwingine Sila.
sw.R: Lameki alioa wanawake wawili. Mmoja aliitwa Ada, na mwingine aliitwa Sila.

decisions.choice: two wives: the first time a man marries more than one woman
decisions.reason: Lamech is the first man in the Bible to have two wives, a departure from the one flesh of 2:24. The text reports it without comment, but the story of Lamech that follows is one of pride and violence.

source.text: וַתֵּ֥לֶד עָדָ֖ה אֶת־יָבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And bore Adah Jabal; he was [the] father of dwellers [in] tent and livestock.

en.L: And Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and [have] livestock.
en.B: Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.
en.R: Adah had a son named Jabal. He was the first of the people who live in tents and raise animals.

es.L: Y Ada dio a luz a Jabal; él fue el padre de los que habitan en tiendas y [tienen] ganado.
es.B: Ada dio a luz a Jabal, que fue el padre de los que viven en tiendas y crían ganado.
es.R: Ada tuvo un hijo llamado Jabal. Él fue el primero de los que viven en tiendas de campaña y crían animales.

fr.L: Et Ada enfanta Jabal ; il fut le père de ceux qui habitent sous la tente et [ont] du bétail.
fr.B: Ada donna naissance à Jabal. Il fut le père de ceux qui vivent sous la tente et élèvent du bétail.
fr.R: Ada a eu un fils appelé Jabal. Il a été le premier des gens qui vivent sous des tentes et qui élèvent des animaux.

sw.L: Naye Ada akamzaa Yabali; yeye alikuwa baba wa wakaao katika hema na [wenye] mifugo.
sw.B: Ada alimzaa Yabali. Yeye alikuwa baba wa wale wanaoishi katika hema na kufuga wanyama.
sw.R: Ada alipata mtoto wa kiume aliyeitwa Yabali. Yeye alikuwa wa kwanza kati ya watu wanaoishi katika hema na kufuga wanyama.

decisions.choice: father of: the founder of a way of life
decisions.reason: "Father" here means the first of a group or the founder of a craft, not only an ancestor (as in 2 Kings 2:12 of the prophets' leader).

decisions.choice: tiendas de campaña
decisions.reason: Readable says "tiendas de campaña" because "tiendas" alone usually means shops in everyday Spanish.

decisions.choice: Ada, Tsilla, Jabal, Joubal, Toubal-Caïn, Naama (verses 19-22)
decisions.reason: French transcribes the Hebrew sounds of these names: "ts" for the sound English writes "z" in Zillah, and "ou" where French spelling would otherwise misread "u"; the Hebrew "y" is written "J", as in the other names of Genesis (Jared, Jacob, Jobab).

decisions.choice: Ada, Sila, Yabali, Yubali, Tubal-kaini, Naama (verses 19-22)
decisions.reason: Swahili forms ending in a vowel, with "y" for the Hebrew "j" sound. "Tubal-kaini" keeps "Kaini", the Swahili form of Cain, inside the name.

source.text: וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יוּבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כָּל־תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of his brother [was] Jubal; he was [the] father of everyone who plays lyre and pipe.

en.L: And the name of his brother [was] Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and the pipe.
en.B: His brother's name was Jubal. He was the father of all who play the lyre and the flute.
en.R: His brother was named Jubal. He was the first of all the people who play music on harps and flutes.

es.L: Y el nombre de su hermano [era] Jubal; él fue el padre de todos los que tocan la lira y la flauta.
es.B: Su hermano se llamaba Jubal. Él fue el padre de todos los que tocan la lira y la flauta.
es.R: Su hermano se llamaba Jubal. Él fue el primero de todos los que hacen música con arpas y flautas.

fr.L: Et le nom de son frère [était] Joubal ; il fut le père de tous ceux qui jouent de la lyre et de la flûte.
fr.B: Son frère s’appelait Joubal. Il fut le père de tous ceux qui jouent de la lyre et de la flûte.
fr.R: Son frère s’appelait Joubal. Il a été le premier de tous ceux qui font de la musique avec la harpe et la flûte.

sw.L: Na jina la nduguye [lilikuwa] Yubali; yeye alikuwa baba wa wote wapigao kinubi na filimbi.
sw.B: Ndugu yake aliitwa Yubali. Yeye alikuwa baba wa wote wanaopiga kinubi na filimbi.
sw.R: Ndugu yake aliitwa Yubali. Yeye alikuwa wa kwanza kati ya watu wote wanaopiga muziki kwa vinubi na filimbi.

decisions.choice: lyre and pipe: a stringed and a wind instrument
decisions.reason: The first is a lyre, a small handheld stringed instrument (David's "harp", 1 Samuel 16:23). The second is probably a pipe or flute. Together they stand for all music.

source.text: וְצִלָּ֣ה גַם־הִ֗וא יָֽלְדָה֙ אֶת־תּ֣וּבַל קַ֔יִן לֹטֵ֕שׁ כָּל־חֹרֵ֥שׁ נְחֹ֖שֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֑ל וַֽאֲח֥וֹת תּֽוּבַל־קַ֖יִן נַֽעֲמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Zillah, also she bore Tubal-cain, a forger of every cutting [tool] of bronze and iron. And [the] sister of Tubal-cain [was] Naamah.

en.L: And Zillah also bore Tubal-cain, a forger of every tool of bronze and iron; and the sister of Tubal-cain [was] Naamah.
en.B: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.
en.R: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-cain. He made all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain had a sister named Naamah.

es.L: Y Zila, también ella dio a luz a Tubal-caín, forjador de toda herramienta de bronce y de hierro; y la hermana de Tubal-caín [era] Naamá.
es.B: Zila también tuvo un hijo, Tubal-caín, que forjaba toda clase de herramientas de bronce y de hierro. La hermana de Tubal-caín fue Naamá.
es.R: Zila también tuvo un hijo, Tubal-caín. Él hacía toda clase de herramientas de bronce y de hierro. Tubal-caín tenía una hermana llamada Naamá.

fr.L: Et Tsilla, elle aussi, enfanta Toubal-Caïn, forgeron de tout outil de bronze et de fer ; et la sœur de Toubal-Caïn [était] Naama.
fr.B: Tsilla, elle aussi, eut un fils, Toubal-Caïn, qui forgeait toutes sortes d’outils en bronze et en fer. La sœur de Toubal-Caïn était Naama.
fr.R: Tsilla aussi a eu un fils, Toubal-Caïn. Il fabriquait toutes sortes d’outils en bronze et en fer. Toubal-Caïn avait une sœur, qui s’appelait Naama.

sw.L: Naye Sila, yeye pia akamzaa Tubal-kaini, mfuaji wa kila chombo cha shaba na chuma; na dada yake Tubal-kaini [alikuwa] Naama.
sw.B: Sila naye alimzaa mtoto wa kiume, Tubal-kaini, aliyefua kila aina ya vyombo vya shaba na chuma. Dada yake Tubal-kaini alikuwa Naama.
sw.R: Sila pia alipata mtoto wa kiume, Tubal-kaini. Alitengeneza kila aina ya vifaa vya shaba na chuma. Tubal-kaini alikuwa na dada aliyeitwa Naama.

decisions.choice: a forger of every tool of bronze and iron: a metalworker
alternatives: a sharpener of every cutting tool
decisions.reason: The words mean one who hammers or sharpens metal and one who works it. Bronze and iron stand for metal working in general; the account names the first of the crafts without fixing a date for them.

decisions.choice: Naamah: named without a story
decisions.reason: Naamah ("pleasant") is one of the few women named in these genealogies. Nothing more is told of her.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לֶ֜מֶךְ לְנָשָׁ֗יו עָדָ֤ה וְצִלָּה֙ שְׁמַ֣עַן קוֹלִ֔י נְשֵׁ֣י לֶ֔מֶךְ הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ הָרַ֨גְתִּי֙ לְפִצְעִ֔י וְיֶ֖לֶד לְחַבֻּרָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Lamech to his wives, Adah and Zillah, hear my voice, wives of Lamech, give ear to my word: for a man I have killed for my wound, and a young man for my bruise.

en.L: And Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my word: for I have killed a man for wounding me, and a young man for striking me.
en.B: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamech, hear my words: I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
en.R: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me! Wives of Lamech, hear what I say! A man hurt me, so I killed him. A young man struck me, so I killed him.

es.L: Y dijo Lamec a sus mujeres: «Ada y Zila, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}} mi voz; mujeres de Lamec, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} mi palabra: porque a un hombre he matado por herirme, y a un joven por golpearme.
es.B: Lamec dijo a sus esposas: «Ada y Zila, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}; esposas de Lamec, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}} mis palabras: he matado a un hombre por herirme, a un joven por golpearme.
es.R: Lamec les dijo a sus esposas: «¡Ada y Zila, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}! ¡Esposas de Lamec, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}} lo que digo! Un hombre me hirió, y yo lo maté. Un joven me golpeó, y yo lo maté.

fr.L: Et Lamech dit à ses femmes : « Ada et Tsilla, entendez ma voix ; femmes de Lamech, prêtez l’oreille à ma parole : car j’ai tué un homme pour m’avoir blessé, et un jeune homme pour m’avoir frappé.
fr.B: Lamech dit à ses femmes : « Ada et Tsilla, écoutez-moi ; femmes de Lamech, entendez mes paroles : j’ai tué un homme parce qu’il m’avait blessé, un jeune homme parce qu’il m’avait frappé.
fr.R: Lamech a dit à ses femmes : « Ada et Tsilla, écoutez-moi ! Femmes de Lamech, écoutez ce que je dis ! Un homme m’a blessé, alors je l’ai tué. Un jeune homme m’a frappé, alors je l’ai tué.

sw.L: Naye Lameki akawaambia wake zake, "Ada na Sila, sikieni sauti yangu; wake wa Lameki, tegeni sikio kwa neno langu: kwa maana nimemuua mtu kwa kunijeruhi, na kijana kwa kunipiga.
sw.B: Lameki akawaambia wake zake, "Ada na Sila, nisikilizeni; wake wa Lameki, sikieni maneno yangu: nimemuua mtu kwa sababu alinijeruhi, kijana kwa sababu alinipiga.
sw.R: Lameki akawaambia wake zake, "Ada na Sila, nisikilizeni! Wake wa Lameki, sikieni ninachosema! Mtu mmoja aliniumiza, nami nikamuua. Kijana mmoja alinipiga, nami nikamuua.

decisions.choice: Lamech's song: the first poem of a human after the garden is a boast
decisions.reason: The verse is poetry, in pairs of lines that say the same thing twice. Where the man's first words were joy at the woman (2:23), Lamech's are a boast of revenge.

decisions.choice: I have killed a man for wounding me: an act already done
alternatives: I will kill any man who wounds me (a threat)
decisions.reason: The verb has a completed form and most likely reports a killing. Some read it as a threat. Either way, Lamech takes a life for a wound: vengeance far beyond the harm.

decisions.choice: a man ... a young man: one victim, described twice
decisions.reason: In Hebrew poetry the second line usually repeats the first in other words, so "a man" and "a young man" are probably the same person.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}}, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}
decisions.reason: Lamech speaks to both wives, so the commands are plural and take the plural "you" setting: ustedes forms by default, vosotros forms with the setting. English imperatives show no number, so the English has no span here. The song keeps its paired lines (meaning decision m1) at every level.

source.text: כִּ֥י שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקַּם־קָ֑יִן וְלֶ֖מֶךְ שִׁבְעִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For sevenfold Cain will be avenged, and Lamech seventy and seven.

en.L: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."
en.B: If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech seventy-seven times!"
en.R: If anyone who kills Cain will be punished seven times as much, then anyone who hurts me will be punished seventy-seven times as much!"

es.L: Si Caín es vengado siete veces, entonces Lamec setenta y siete veces».
es.B: Si Caín es vengado siete veces, ¡Lamec lo será setenta y siete!».
es.R: Si a quien mate a Caín se le castigará siete veces más, ¡a quien me haga daño a mí se le castigará setenta y siete veces más!».

fr.L: Si Caïn est vengé sept fois, Lamech [le sera] soixante-dix-sept fois. »
fr.B: Si Caïn est vengé sept fois, Lamech le sera soixante-dix-sept fois ! »
fr.R: Si celui qui tue Caïn doit être puni sept fois plus, celui qui me fait du mal sera puni soixante-dix-sept fois plus ! »

sw.L: Ikiwa Kaini atalipiziwa kisasi mara saba, basi Lameki mara sabini na saba."
sw.B: Ikiwa Kaini atalipiziwa kisasi mara saba, Lameki atalipiziwa mara sabini na saba!"
sw.R: Ikiwa mtu atakayemuua Kaini ataadhibiwa mara saba zaidi, basi mtu atakayeniumiza mimi ataadhibiwa mara sabini na saba zaidi!"

decisions.choice: seventy-seven: unlimited vengeance, reversed by Jesus
decisions.reason: Lamech turns God's protection of Cain (verse 15) into a boast of endless revenge. Jesus reverses the number when he tells Peter to forgive "seventy-seven times" (Matthew 18:22, where the Greek can also be read "seventy times seven").

decisions.choice: If ... then
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can mean "for" or "if"; English reads the comparison more clearly with "if ... then".

decisions.choice: atalipiziwa kisasi
decisions.reason: Swahili distinguishes the one on whose behalf vengeance is taken ("kulipiziwa kisasi", here Cain and Lamech) from the one on whom it falls ("kulipizwa kisasi", the killer in 4:15).

source.text: וַיֵּ֨דַע אָדָ֥ם עוֹד֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁ֑ת כִּ֣י שָֽׁת־לִ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ זֶ֣רַע אַחֵ֔ר תַּ֣חַת הֶ֔בֶל כִּ֥י הֲרָג֖וֹ קָֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: And knew Adam again his wife, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, for has appointed to me God another offspring in place of Abel, for Cain killed him.

en.L: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, "For God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
en.B: Adam was intimate with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has given me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
en.R: Adam and his wife had another son. She named him Seth. She said, "God has given me another child to take the place of Abel, because Cain killed him."

es.L: Y conoció Adán otra vez a su mujer, y ella dio a luz un hijo y llamó su nombre Set: «Porque Dios me ha puesto otra descendencia en lugar de Abel, pues Caín lo mató».
es.B: Adán se unió de nuevo a su esposa, y ella dio a luz un hijo al que llamó Set, diciendo: «Dios me ha dado otro hijo en lugar de Abel, ya que Caín lo mató».
es.R: Adán y su esposa tuvieron otro hijo. Ella lo llamó Set, y dijo: «Dios me ha dado otro hijo que ocupe el lugar de Abel, porque Caín lo mató».

fr.L: Et Adam connut encore sa femme ; elle enfanta un fils et appela son nom Seth : « Car Dieu m’a établi une autre descendance à la place d’Abel, parce que Caïn l’a tué. »
fr.B: Adam s’unit de nouveau à sa femme ; elle donna naissance à un fils et l’appela Seth, en disant : « Dieu m’a accordé un autre enfant à la place d’Abel, puisque Caïn l’a tué. »
fr.R: Adam et sa femme ont eu un autre fils. Elle l’a appelé Seth. Elle a dit : « Dieu m’a donné un autre enfant pour remplacer Abel, parce que Caïn l’a tué. »

sw.L: Naye Adamu akamjua mkewe tena, naye akamzaa mwana, akamwita jina lake Sethi, "Kwa maana Mungu ameniwekea uzao mwingine mahali pa Habili, kwa sababu Kaini alimuua."
sw.B: Adamu alikutana kimwili na mkewe tena, naye akamzaa mtoto wa kiume, akamwita Sethi, akisema, "Mungu amenipa mtoto mwingine mahali pa Habili, kwa kuwa Kaini alimuua."
sw.R: Adamu na mkewe walipata mtoto mwingine wa kiume. Mkewe alimwita Sethi. Akasema, "Mungu amenipa mtoto mwingine achukue nafasi ya Habili, kwa sababu Kaini alimuua."

decisions.choice: Adam: here a personal name
decisions.reason: The word that meant "the man" or "humankind" is used here without the article, plainly as a name. From here on the first man is called Adam (5:1-5).

decisions.choice: Seth: a name that sounds like "appointed"
decisions.reason: Eve explains the name Seth (shet) by the verb shat, "he has appointed" or "granted".

decisions.choice: another offspring: the line continues after Abel's death
decisions.reason: The word is "seed", the word of 3:15. Through Seth the line of promise goes on, the line Genesis 5 follows to Noah.

decisions.choice: "For God has appointed for me ..."
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say "she said"; Literal puts Eve's words in quotation marks after "For", as her reason for the name.

source.text: וּלְשֵׁ֤ת גַּם־הוּא֙ יֻלַּד־בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱנ֑וֹשׁ אָ֣ז הוּחַ֔ל לִקְרֹ֖א בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And to Seth, also to him was born a son, and he called his name Enosh. Then it was begun to call on [the] name of YHWH.

en.L: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. Then [people] began to call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. That was when people began to pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worship him by name.

es.L: Y a Set, también a él le nació un hijo, y llamó su nombre Enós. Entonces se comenzó a invocar el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Set también tuvo un hijo, y lo llamó Enós. En aquel tiempo la gente comenzó a invocar el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Set también tuvo un hijo, y le puso por nombre Enós. Fue entonces cuando la gente comenzó a orar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y a adorar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.

fr.L: Et à Seth, à lui aussi, naquit un fils, et il appela son nom Énosh. Alors on commença à invoquer le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Seth eut lui aussi un fils, qu’il appela Énosh. C’est à cette époque que l’on commença à invoquer le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Seth aussi a eu un fils, et il l’a appelé Énosh. C’est à ce moment-là que les gens ont commencé à prier {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et à {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorer en {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appelant par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.

sw.L: Naye Sethi, yeye pia, akapata mwana, akamwita jina lake Enoshi. Ndipo [watu] wakaanza kuliitia jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Sethi naye alipata mtoto wa kiume, akamwita Enoshi. Wakati huo watu walianza kuliitia jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Sethi naye alipata mtoto wa kiume, akamwita Enoshi. Wakati huo ndipo watu walipoanza kumwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kumwabudu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.

decisions.choice: Enosh: a word for a human being
decisions.reason: Enosh is a poetic word for a human being, often stressing frailty (Psalm 8:5; 103:15).

decisions.choice: to call on the name of the LORD: to worship him and pray to him
decisions.reason: To call on the LORD's name is to worship and pray to him (12:8; Psalm 116:17). In contrast with the line of Cain, the line of Seth turns to the LORD. Exodus 6:3 says God made himself known by this name to Moses in a new way; here the narrator uses the name for the worship of the earliest people.

decisions.choice: [people] began
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it was begun", with no subject; Literal brackets "people".

decisions.choice: pray to the LORD and worship him by name
alternatives: call on the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what calling on the LORD's name means (m2).

decisions.choice: se comenzó a invocar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb has no subject ("it was begun"). Spanish can say this with the impersonal "se", so Literal needs no bracketed subject, where the English Literal supplies "[people]".

decisions.choice: a orar al SEÑOR y a adorar su nombre
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable says what calling on the name means (meaning decision m2). "Adorar su nombre" lets the deity pronoun setting fall on "su"; Spanish attaches "lo" to the verb in "adorarlo", where a setting span cannot sit.

decisions.choice: Alors on commença
decisions.reason: French impersonal "on" says "it was begun" without naming anyone, as the Hebrew does, so Literal needs no bracketed subject where the English brackets "[people]".
